title: Executable Constraints
motto: Instructions written as prose are wishes. Instructions written as constraints are tests. The workbench turns each rule into something an agent can check at runtime and a reviewer can verify after the fact.

steps.title: Core idea
steps.body: Instructions written as prose are wishes. Instructions written as constraints are tests. The workbench turns each rule into something an agent can check at runtime and a reviewer can verify after the fact.

steps.title: Why this matters
cards: A typical `AGENTS.md` reads like onboarding documentation. It tells the agent to "be careful" and "test thoroughly" and "ask if unsure." Three days later, the agent ships a change with no tests, writes to a forbidden directory, and never asks because it never knew where the line was.
Instructions are powerful when they are operational and weak when they are aspirational. The fix is to write rules the workbench can interpret and the reviewer can score.

steps.title: The concept
steps.body: Treat instructions as verifiable contracts on agent behavior.

steps.title: Implement wb33
steps.body: Write the function from scratch in the workspace. Run when ready — all tests must pass.

code.starter:
def constraint_ok(output, forbidden):
    return not any(f in output for f in forbidden)
